clue.text: Fixing this bangle is difficult

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters of these three words are hard to manage and get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to fasten a bracelet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' is the anagram signal; the letters of THIS BANGLE IS rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixing a date or a fact is settling or setting it up firmly, a synonym.

clue.text: The Avengers came to Ireland, we affirm

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
an affirmative answer is yes

explanation.surface: A team of TV avengers pays a visit to Ireland, and we confirm it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came to' just joins the two pieces. The Avengers here are not the TV show but the Furies of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the Furies were goddesses of vengeance, also called by this Greek name.

clue.text: Go on, Brown, dance!

indicators.note: in this down clue 'Go on Brown' puts the verb on top of the colour word in the column, so it follows it in reading order

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone urges a man called Brown to get up and dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a man's surname being urged to dance, but it is only the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tango is a ballroom dance of Argentine origin.

clue.text: At least they don't have to sew on their own buttons!

definitions.text: At least they don't have to sew on their own buttons!

parts.words: At least they don't have to sew on their own buttons!
parts.note: the clue pretends to describe lucky people with a helper, but it is ironic: these are unmarried men who have no wife to do their mending

explanation.surface: A grumble about who does the household mending.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that the people described have no one to sew for them: unmarried men had to do it themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarried men, traditionally lacking a wife to mend their clothes, are the group meant.

clue.text: They show signs of business going with a swing

definitions.text: They show signs of business going with a swing

parts.words: They show signs of business going with a swing
parts.note: 'going with a swing' usually means thriving, but here the signboards hanging outside pubs literally swing in the wind

explanation.surface: Successful firms show signs of booming trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Pubs and hotels traditionally hang painted signboards that swing; 'going with a swing' sounds like a business doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: Public houses and hotels advertise with hanging painted signboards, so they display swinging signs of trade.

clue.text: Though not drunk, they give Elspeth a lot of trouble

indicators.note: the letters of the name and the article are put into disorder, as if troubled

explanation.surface: A sober woman named Elspeth still finds some things troublesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give ... a lot of trouble' signals the anagram of ELSPETH plus A. 'drunk' suggests drunkenness, but it is the past participle: the remains left undrunk in a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the dregs of liquor left in the bottom of a glass, the part not swallowed.

clue.text: Abroad, this prize elevates the good

indicators.note: in a down clue raising the words lifts them so they are read from bottom up

parts.note: in French, 'le bon' means 'the good', which 'Abroad' signals

explanation.surface: A prize awarded overseas honours virtuous people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' tells us to put 'the good' into French, LE BON; 'elevates' turns it upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish awards for peace, literature and science carry the name of their founder, Alfred.

clue.text: What an angry father's shotgun has to say about the sea

indicators.note: what is said is the spoken message, so the letters are taken from how the phrase sounds

parts.note: a shotgun wedding: the furious father's gun announces that it is time to wed

explanation.surface: An outraged dad levels his gun at a daughter's seducer, with something to say about the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shotgun wedding' is forced by an angry father; his gun's message is 'Marry time!', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime means relating to the sea or seafaring, as in maritime law.

clue.text: A compact distance

definitions.meaning: a compact is an agreement or alliance between parties
an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: Something small and portable that covers ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is both an alliance of states and an obsolete unit of length of roughly three miles.

clue.text: In no way, we hear, could this be to blame

indicators.note: says the words are spoken, so the letters come from their sound

parts.note: in no way means in no sense

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a thing cannot possibly be at fault.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a statement: 'in no sense' could this be blameworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free from guilt is the opposite of being blameworthy, so this quality could never be at fault.

clue.text: The mark of the beast that marks the trail

definitions.meaning: a white stripe down the face of a horse or cow
a mark cut on a tree trunk to show a path

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding sign of evil that also guides travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The mark of the beast' sounds like the Book of Revelation, but the beast is just a horse with a white face stripe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a pale facial stripe on an animal and a notch cut into bark to waymark a route.

clue.text: The guard find their sphere in an Arab republic

indicators.note: the round letter is placed inside the country's name

parts.note: Yemen is a republic on the Arabian peninsula
a sphere is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Soldiers on guard duty find their place in a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yeomen of the Guard are the British monarch's ceremonial bodyguard; the plural matches 'guard' as a body of men.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yeomen of the Guard form the ceremonial royal bodyguard, so the corps is a guard.

clue.text: Prevarication may be fatal for the P.O.

definitions.meaning: delaying or evading by playing for time

definitions.text: may be fatal for the P.O.
definitions.meaning: a P.O. is a Pilot Officer in the RAF, and an aircraft losing lift can crash

explanation.surface: Dithering can cost a pilot officer dearly.
explanation.walkthrough: P.O. is Pilot Officer, an RAF rank; an aeroplane that loses airspeed and lift is said to do this.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing for time is evasion, and an aircraft losing lift through low airspeed can crash.

clue.text: Arden's singular stonecrop?

parts.note: in As You Like It, set in the Forest of Arden, the exiled Duke finds '... in stones', so one of them is a crop grown from stone

explanation.surface: A gardener asks about a rock plant from the Forest of Arden.
explanation.walkthrough: Stonecrop is a real plant, which misleads; Shakespeare's Duke Senior speaks of 'books in the running brooks, sermons in stones', and the singular of those is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line says stones yield moral lessons, so a single homily is what Arden's stones produce.

clue.text: Flute for an angel ?

definitions.meaning: a simple wooden woodwind pipe played end-on
the recording angel notes down people's deeds for Judgement Day

explanation.surface: A musical instrument suited to a heavenly being.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an end-blown woodwind instrument and also the angel who writes down every soul's deeds.

clue.text: Unusual for vipers to be so playful!

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the letters of the two words is called for

explanation.surface: Snakes behaving in a frisky way would be odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' is the anagram signal for VIPERS TO; 'be so' joins to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportive means frolicsome and fond of fun, a synonym.

clue.text: Setting for a brotherly board meeting

definitions.text: Setting for a brotherly board meeting

parts.words: Setting for a brotherly board meeting
parts.note: the board is a dining table, not a committee, and the brothers are monks gathering to eat

explanation.surface: A venue for a friendly directors' meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a company board, but it is the old sense of a table laid with food; the brothers are monks.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery's dining hall is where monks gather at table for meals.

clue.text: The county has its share of the right crowd

parts.note: some means a share or portion of something
R is the abbreviation for right
a set is a group or clique of people

explanation.surface: A county gets its fair portion of decent folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The right crowd' looks like one phrase, but splits into R and SET. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an English shire in the south-west, an example of a county.

clue.text: Dollars dishonestly acquired at the staghunt ?

parts.note: buck is slang for a dollar
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Money gained by cheating at a deer hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: this lead shot is what is fired at deer in a staghunt, and 'bucks' are also male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse lead pellets fired from a shotgun are used for hunting deer.

clue.text: Laissez-faire advice for recovery of her charges

definitions.text: Laissez-faire advice for recovery of her charges

parts.words: Laissez-faire advice for recovery of her charges
parts.note: the nursery rhyme shepherdess lost her sheep and was told to leave them alone and they would come home

explanation.surface: Hands-off guidance to someone trying to get back the people in her care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laissez-faire' means leave alone; in the nursery rhyme the shepherdess is told 'Leave them alone, and they'll come home'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme the little shepherdess who lost her sheep is advised to do nothing to get them back.

clue.text: One has cause to produce this

definitions.text: One has cause to produce this

parts.words: One has cause to produce this
parts.note: a cause, by definition, brings about a result

explanation.surface: Someone has good reason to bring something out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has cause to' sounds like 'has reason to', but read as 'cause and ...', the familiar pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: The result brought about by a cause is its consequence, the second half of 'cause and ...'.

clue.text: The Marines have a new driver? That's so much hot air!

parts.note: taken as written
RM stands for Royal Marines
a learner driver displays an L plate

explanation.surface: Boasting that the Marines have a new recruit behind the wheel is empty talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot air' means empty talk in the surface, but here is literal: a rising current of warm air. In Britain a learner driver shows an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising column of warmed air, used by gliders and birds, is literally a body of heated air.

clue.text: Having spotted animal on East river he told his tale

parts.note: pard is an old word for a leopard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who saw a leopard by the East River recounts his story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East river' suggests New York's East River, but splits into E and R. The definition refers to one of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims, a seller of indulgences, tells a tale in the Canterbury Tales.

clue.text: Attack, toss a stone!

indicators.note: tossing the word throws its letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: An order to attack by throwing a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toss' is the anagram signal for STONE; 'a' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the start of an assault, a charge or attack.

clue.text: A bit of a drip, this hanger-on at the house-warming?

definitions.text: A bit of a drip, this hanger-on at the house-warming?

parts.words: A bit of a drip, this hanger-on at the house-warming?
parts.note: the dull guest at a party is really frozen water hanging from the eaves, dripping as the house warms up

explanation.surface: A dreary freeloader at a party for a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drip' (a bore) and 'hanger-on' (a sponger) are both literal: something hanging from the roof that drips when the house warms.
explanation.definitionFit: A spike of frozen water hangs from a roof and drips as it melts in the warmth.

clue.text: Go up, as the pretentious are forced to go down?

definitions.text: Go up, as the pretentious are forced to go down?

parts.words: Go up, as the pretentious are forced to go down?
parts.note: social upstarts rise, and when humbled are made to back down, which uses the same verb with 'down'

explanation.surface: The pompous rise and are made to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Social climbers go up; when they are made to back down they are said to do this 'down' too.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to mount upwards, and to back down humbly is the same verb with 'down'.

clue.text: Satanic brood of one chemist

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
MPS stands for Member of the Pharmaceutical Society, a qualified chemist

explanation.surface: The devil's offspring descended from a single pharmacist.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a chemist is a pharmacist; MPS was the letters after a pharmacist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Little devils are the mischievous offspring of Satan.

clue.text: One against one among the Seven Sleepers

indicators.note: the letters lie among the words, running across them

explanation.surface: One person faces another among the legendary Seven Sleepers.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'Seven Sleepers', the legendary youths who slept in a cave for centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting odds of one to one, a stake against an equal stake, are called this.

clue.text: M.P. you miss, oddly enough, at the conference

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an odd, unexpected way

explanation.surface: An MP is missed at a meeting, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' is the anagram signal for MP YOU MISS; 'at' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A symposium is a meeting for discussion, a conference.

clue.text: Notwithstanding you can't have one ?

parts.note: split as 'not with standing': without social standing you cannot own the badge of prestige

explanation.surface: Even so, you are told you can't have one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notwithstanding' looks like 'despite', but read as 'not with standing': without social position you cannot have an emblem of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A possession displayed to show prestige requires the social rank it advertises.
